extracted.intended_audience: marketing researchers and practitioners / content creators interested in online virality
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical findings about which emotional and content features increase the likelihood that online content will be shared (i.e., go viral), aimed at informing viral marketing campaign design and related research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valence (positive vs negative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive content is more viral than negative content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat valence as the only predictor — the paper notes 'the relationship between emotion and social transmission is more complex than valence alone.' Use valence as one axis but consider arousal/activation and other features as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation / Arousal level
rubrics_metrics.description: Virality is driven, in part, by activation and arousal: content that evokes high arousal tends to be more viral than content that evokes low arousal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-arousal emotions (whether positive or negative) increase social transmission; low-arousal or deactivating emotions decrease it. Design content to provoke activation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-arousal positive emotions (awe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that evokes high-arousal positive emotions — specifically awe — tends to be more viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awe is given as the exemplar of a high-arousal positive emotion that increases sharing. Use inspiring, surprising, or grandeur-evoking elements to elicit awe.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-arousal negative emotions (anger, anxiety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that evokes high-arousal negative emotions such as anger or anxiety tends to be more viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anger and anxiety function via high activation to drive sharing; raising concern or moral outrage can increase social transmission, but ethical and brand risks should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-arousal / deactivating emotions (sadness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that evokes low-arousal or deactivating emotions (e.g., sadness) tends to be less viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid purely low-arousal emotional tones if the objective is to maximize sharing; sad or contemplative content may underperform in social transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising content
rubrics_metrics.description: Content perceived as surprising is positively linked to virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unexpected twists, novel facts, or formats that violate expectations to increase the likelihood of sharing; surprise is listed alongside interest and usefulness as drivers of virality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interesting content
rubrics_metrics.description: Content judged as interesting is positively linked to virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize content that captures curiosity or provides engaging narratives; interesting material motivates people to pass it along.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that is practically useful is positively linked to virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable tips, useful information, or utilities that audiences want to save/share; perceived practical value increases social transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: External drivers of attention (prominence / featured placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: External drivers of attention — for example, how prominently content is featured — affect virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement, editorial prominence, and other exogenous attention signals can increase sharing independently of content features; combine content design with distribution/prominence strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design implication: incorporate emotional effects into campaign design
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking the effect of emotions into account helps to design effective viral marketing campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the empirical patterns (valence, arousal, surprise, interest, usefulness, and prominence) when crafting content and campaign strategies to improve chances of virality; balance emotional activation with ethical/brand considerations.
